name: Santa's Countdown
author: BigC07
description: An animated countdown to Christmas for kids: Santa's sleigh and reindeer, waving snowmen, bouncing presents, dancing gingerbread men, flashing lights, Santa stuck in a chimney, elves throwing presents, building one in their workshop and loading the sleigh, Santa and an elf trimming the tree, a candy-cane clock that ticks, an advent calendar, Santa's Nice List with your kids' names, and a Santa tracker for Christmas Eve -- a different scene each time it comes round. All art drawn in code; no network.

versions.notes: Three new scenes, fourteen in all: an advent calendar (24 numbered doors in red and green; the days gone show their pictures and today's door swings open, all shut till December 1), Santa's Nice List (he holds up a scroll, writes each name in and ticks it, then checks it twice; three or more names roll up the scroll a line a second; the names come from a new nice_list setting, EVERYONE if empty), and a Santa tracker for Christmas Eve, worked out from the clock alone: a world map where Santa flies west with midnight from 10:00 UTC on the 24th, the places he has been lighting up with gold, with where he is and how long till he reaches you; till then, the days to take-off. New settings home_name and home_location mark home on the map. The loading elves balance each present on their hat instead of lifting it overhead on long arms, with space between the pile, the elves and the sleigh.

Three new scenes, eleven in all: elves loading Santa's parked sleigh (the stack beside them goes down as the tower in the sleigh goes up), Santa and an elf trimming the tree (ornaments, then the elf puts the star on top and it lights up), and a clock -- the time in rolling candy-cane stripes, ticking every second while it scrolls, centred over the date and the days to go, with a new time_format setting (12h or 24h). Every tree gets a seven-wide steady gold star in place of a five-pixel plus that flashed and read as a cross; the snowmen are bigger and their hat shows (grey with a red band and holly, not black); Rudolph's nose is red only. No two elf scenes ever come back to back.

Taller panels: the rows above and below the card get the scene's sky -- falling snow or twinkling stars, in dots the size of the card's -- instead of plain black, and the snowman's ground runs to the bottom of the panel. A doubled card always keeps at least 64 columns, so a 64x64 panel shows the 64-wide card rather than a cramped 32-wide one. The workshop gets a narrow layout: below 96 columns one elf hammers at a short bench, from 96 both elves work.

First release. Eight animated scenes drawn in code -- sleigh, snowman, presents, gingerbread, lights, chimney, elves, workshop -- shown in turn (or at random), with the days left until Christmas, and MERRY CHRISTMAS! on the day. Shows from season_start (1 November by default) through Christmas Day and stays off the rest of the year. In Vegas it is one live element the ticker redraws in place, so the card animates while it scrolls (core 3.8.0+; older cores get a still frame), and it moves to the next scene every lap, even with nothing else in the rotation.
